comparator.sourceNotes: The current VU Amsterdam curriculum defines the location-specific joint VU-UT programme as six consecutive semesters and lists the complete disciplinary content of each semester. VU states that most teaching is in Amsterdam with recurring laboratory work in Enschede; students enrol at the University of Twente for the UT Mechanical Engineering degree. The official UT current-student curriculum establishes that the three-year Mechanical Engineering bachelor totals 180 EC, or 60 EC per year. The six official semester blocks are therefore recorded at 30 EC each, preserving all 180 EC and the genuine open minor semester without inventing course-level weights that VU does not publish on the page.

exception.reason: The Amsterdam VU-UT Mechanical Engineering bachelor builds four compulsory semesters around mechanics of materials, manufacturing and metals; thermodynamics and renewable-energy engineering; mass manufacturing, polymers, tribology, dynamics and vibrations; and systems, signal, control, precision and finite-element engineering. Its final compulsory semester then adds fluid mechanics, heat transfer, aerodynamic wind-tunnel work and an individual mechanical-engineering research assignment. UCR offers adjacent mathematics, computing, product-design and sustainability courses, but not this mechanical-science core or its laboratory, workshop, prototype, manufacturing and engineering-research progression. A 24-course response would not preserve the programme's academic identity as Mechanical Engineering.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official Amsterdam curriculum accounts for the 180-EC UT degree through six 30-EC semesters. Semesters one through four provide the compulsory mechanical-engineering sequence, semester five is genuine open minor space, and semester six is compulsory scientific research in mechanical engineering. This Amsterdam location has its own semester themes and course sequence rather than simply reproducing the Enschede modules, and it has no named graduation route requiring selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative tools, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming adds computing. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design covers customer-needs analysis, fabrication planning and prototyping; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address environmental impact and sustainable-energy assessment. The workbook contains no statics, mechanics-of-materials or elasticity course; no thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics or heat-transfer sequence; no metals, polymers, manufacturing, tribology, dynamics, vibration, precision-mechanism, control-engineering or finite-element course; and no mechanical-engineering laboratory, workshop, wind-tunnel, integrated design-project or graduation-research sequence. Linear Systems is a useful adjacent signals-and-systems course, but one such course cannot substitute for the semester-scale mechatronics and mechanical-design progression.
